pos.personaBrief: Brighton averaged about 60% possession and had 70%+ games, but De Zerbi treats the ball as bait and says possession depends on opponent pressure; the aim is danger via quick vertical strikes.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up from keeper and centre-backs with studs on the ball, accepting risk under pressure, then switching gears to find the front line fast.

est.personaBrief: Fluid 4-2-3-1 with inverting full-backs, shunted keeper, dropping pivot and tight triangles; fluid positioning around a nominal shape.

lar.personaBrief: Maximum width after pulling the press, overloads in wide areas and Mitoma on the flank, but full-backs invert and central combinations feature too.

blo.personaBrief: Aggressive high line, man-to-man high pressing, PPDA among the lowest in the league, forwards press the centre-backs.

mar.personaBrief: Man-to-man pressing across the pitch with players following their opponent, and little systematic backline protection.

pla.personaBrief: De Zerbi imposed his model, wanting to leave his imprint and play bold football whoever the opponent, with only mild adjustments.

res.personaBrief: Bold, brave, risky football, conceding plenty and sometimes sacrificing results for the style; never sat back.

sis.personaBrief: A strong collective model with drilled patterns and roles for all, built on technical players fitted to the system.

jog.personaBrief: Prioritises highly technical, press-resistant midfielders (Gilmour, Mac Allister, Caicedo), while demanding high-intensity pressing.

bas.personaBrief: Brighton buys young undervalued talents from abroad and sells them on; academy is not the core and development matters.

lid.personaBrief: Little evidence on people management; coach with a firm idea who expects the players to fit it, an authority figure for the model.
